papers.title: Showing versus Doing: Teaching by Demonstration
papers.summary: People often learn from others' demonstrations, and inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) techniques have realized this capacity in machines. In contrast, teaching by demonstration has been less well studied computationally. Here, we develop a Bayesian model for teaching by demonstration. Stark differences arise when demonstrators are intentionally teaching (i.e. showing) a task versus simply performing (i.e. doing) a task. In two experiments, we show that human participants modify their teaching behavior consistent with the predictions of our model. Further, we show that even standard IRL algorithms benefit when learning from showing versus doing.
papers.title_ja: 見せることとすること：デモンストレーションによる教授
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、デモンストレーションによる教授（teaching by demonstration）を計算機科学的にモデル化する研究である。意図的な教授（showing）と単なる実行（doing）では、観測される行動に顕著な違いが生じることを示した。ベイズモデルを用いてこの違いを定式化し、人間の被験者がモデルの予測と一致して教授行動を変更することを2つの実験で検証した。さらに、標準的な逆強化学習（IRL）アルゴリズムも、単なる実行からの学習よりも教授からの学習の方が性能が向上することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習とベイズ推論の手法を含むが、軌道力学やLLM効率化との直接的な関連は薄い。

papers.title: Perfect Reconstruction Cannot Show Whether Two Codebooks on a VAE's Latent Space Agree
papers.summary: Many systems read the latent space of a variational autoencoder (VAE) as discrete codes, and rely on each latent being read back as the code it was written as. Shannon (1948) took such a shared codebook as given; inside a VAE nothing enforces it. We prove that no item of a standard training report can reveal whether the written and read codes agree on encoded data. We construct two VAEs that reconstruct every input perfectly, infer exactly, and match on every per-example ELBO and every code histogram, yet agreement is one in the first and zero in the second. We then show that the ELBO's own terms bound how far a measured agreement can move: the variational gap bounds the shift to exact inference, and the rate bounds the shift to generation from the prior. For Gaussian posteriors, a mean-field encoder pays an exact price in the gap that depends on its choice of axes. On probabilistic PCA the gap certifies a trained encoder in all 75 settings we test, at agreement between 0.76 and 0.97. On 240 trained VAEs, a floor set by the rate and the dataset size rules out rate-side certification in advance for 66 models, and none of them certifies. The results yield a simple protocol, Certify-or-Measure, for any pipeline that reads a VAE as codes.
papers.title_ja: 完全再構成は、VAEの潜在空間における2つのコードブックが一致しているかを示せない
papers.summary_ja: 変分オートエンコーダ（VAE）の潜在空間を離散コードとして読み出す際、書き込みと読み取りのコードが一致していることを標準的な学習指標では検出できないことを証明する。完全再構成とELBOが一致する2つのVAEを構築し、コードの一致度が異なることを示した。ガウス後確率において、変分ギャップとレートが測定された一致度の移動を制限することを示し、確率的PCAではエンコーダの認証が可能だが、多くの学習済みVAEではレート側の認証が不可能であることを実証した。最後に、VAEをコードとして読み出すパイプライン向けの「Certify-or-Measure」プロトコルを提案する。
papers.relevance_reason: VAEの理論的性質に関する研究で、ML手法全般に関わるが、ユーザーの関心であるLLM効率化や軌道力学とは直接関係が薄い。

papers.title: Barycentric Anchored Weight Search for Robust Model Merging
papers.summary: We propose Barycentric Anchored Search, a post-hoc weight-space procedure for improving fine-tuned vision models under distribution shift without additional gradient training or increased inference cost. Given a pre-trained initialization and two checkpoints fine-tuned on a source dataset, the method constructs barycentric candidate weights and performs a small derivative-free search along directions connecting each candidate to the pre-trained model. Candidate weights are selected using a small validation subset of one or more out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets; the selected model is then evaluated on the held-out portions of those datasets, on additional OOD benchmarks, and on the ImageNet validation set to quantify the robustness-accuracy trade-off. The method is inspired by simplex-based derivative-free optimization, including Nelder-Mead and Torczon multidirectional search, but is specialized to the geometry of neural network weight merging. Unlike Model Soup, which typically benefits from many fine-tuned checkpoints, and unlike Model Stock, which applies a fixed geometric merge, our approach uses only two fine-tuned checkpoints and iteratively adapts the merge using validation feedback from OOD data. Experiments with CLIP ViT-B/32 show that the proposed search substantially improves performance on held-out OOD data, including ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-Sketch, while keeping ImageNet accuracy competitive. The resulting weights also improve transfer to OOD datasets not used during candidate selection, outperforming the original fine-tuned checkpoints, naive model soups, and Model Stock in our evaluations. These results suggest that lightweight optimization in anchored weight space provides a practical alternative to fixed weight-averaging rules, geometric merging, or single-model selection.
papers.title_ja: 頑健なモデルマージのための重心アンカー付き重み探索
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、勾配計算や推論コストの増加なしに、分布シフト下での視覚モデルの頑健性を高めるための事後処理手法「Barycentric Anchored Search」を提案する。事前学習済みモデルと2つのファインチューニング済みチェックポイントを用い、重心座標系に基づいた候補重みを生成し、Nelder-Mead法などの導関数なし最適化アルゴリズムを応用して重み空間を探索する。検証セットのフィードバックに基づいて重みを適応的に調整することで、ImageNet-AなどのOODデータセットにおける性能を向上させつつ、ImageNetの精度も維持する。この手法は、固定された幾何学的マージや単純なモデルソープよりも、軽量かつ実用的な代替手段として機能する。
papers.relevance_reason: モデルマージはLLM効率化に関連するが、対象が視覚モデル中心のため直接性は低い

papers.title: Historical Anchors for Scientific Forecasting on Human-Aware Knowledge Graphs
papers.summary: Predicting which scientific connections will form next can point researchers toward the most promising leads. One successful approach learns representations by sampling paths through publication networks, represented by a hypergraph, that connect scientific entities, concepts, and researchers, approximating how knowledge and expertise move through the literature. Sampled paths are then used to train an embedding model to forecast scientific connections such as a property of a material. Performance, however, depends strongly on how many paths are sampled: too little sampling yields incomplete representations, while further sampling can eventually weaken prediction quality. The best sampling budget is therefore often identifiable only after future discoveries are known. We introduce Query--Anchor Agreement (QAA), a diagnostic requiring no future labels or separately trained model. QAA can be used to select a sampling budget, and refine or re-rank the resulting forecast to improve forecasting scientific connections. QAA compares the candidates a model predicts for a target with those most similar to the target's known historical examples, and identifies when these two views converge. Across thermoelectric-material and COVID-19 drug-repurposing benchmarks, repeated random-seed runs, and three sampling policies, QAA-selected budgets fall on average 1.86 percentage points below hindsight-optimal selection for broad candidate recovery. Further, promoting candidates supported by both views, under a capped fusion that bounds the anchor contribution, improves broad recovery across all six benchmark-policy settings, which define the types of network walks used for sampling.
papers.title_ja: 人間認識型ナレッジグラフにおける科学的予測のための歴史的アンカー
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、出版物ネットワークのハイパーグラフからサンプリングされたパスを用いて科学的な関連性を予測する手法の改善を提案する。サンプリング予算が予測性能に大きく影響し、事後最適解が不明確な問題に対し、将来のラベルを必要としない診断指標「Query--Anchor Agreement (QAA)」を導入する。QAAは、モデルの予測候補とターゲットの既知の歴史的類似例の一致度を比較し、最適なサンプリング予算の選択や予測結果のリランキングを行う。熱電材料やCOVID-19薬剤転用などのベンチマークにおいて、QAAによる予算選択は事後最適解に平均1.86ポイントしか届かない高精度を示し、融合手法により広範な候補回復率を向上させることを実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: ML手法と評価指標は関心だが、軌道力学やLLM効率化とは直接無関係

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning from Real-Robot Interaction without High-Quality State Estimates
papers.summary: A longstanding goal for robot reinforcement learning (RL) is that robots learn from their own physical experience, as humans and animals do. A key obstacle to learning directly from physical experience, especially outside instrumented lab environments, is that the state of the world is usually unobservable to the learner and must be estimated from on-board sensing. Errors in that estimate corrupt both the policy input and potentially the reward signal. We study this challenge using the contact-rich task of a bipedal robot learning to score soccer goals. We estimate all key state variables on-board with an unscented Kalman filter (UKF) and no external instrumentation (e.g., motion capture or overhead cameras). Because the UKF may incorrectly estimate state when the ball is unobserved, we learn a new state representation with a recurrent state-space model (RSSM) that, critically, only corrects the RSSM's latent state when the ball is observed. Building on RLPD, we introduce RSSM-RLPD and apply it to the task of a NAO robot learning to dribble a soccer ball into a goal. We show that the robot learns to score from multiple starting positions after 30 minutes of real-world interaction, reaching 100% success against 0% for a feed-forward policy under the same training budget. We complement our physical robot experiments with a simulation study and show that RSSM-RLPD learns policies that achieve a higher success rate than behavior cloning, a feed-forward, and GRU baseline. Taken together, our results show that the addition of a learned state representation to existing on-robot learning methods enables RL from real-robot data even with a high degree of partial observability.
papers.title_ja: 高品質な状態推定なしで実ロボットとの相互作用から強化学習を行う
papers.summary_ja: 実環境における部分観測可能性の問題を解決するため、UKFと再帰状態空間モデル（RSSM）を組み合わせた新しい状態表現手法を提案する。ボールが観測されない際の推定誤差を補正する仕組みにより、NAOロボットが30分の実機学習で100%の成功率を達成した。シミュレーション実験でも、フィードフォワードやGRUベースラインを上回る性能を示し、高品質な外部計測器なしでの強化学習の有効性を証明した。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習と状態推定は関心領域だが、宇宙・軌道力学との直接関連は薄い

papers.title: CopyQuad: Quadrupedal Skill Transfer from a Single Side-View Video Without a Depth Model
papers.summary: Video-to-robot pipelines for quadrupedal imitation insert a learned lifting stage, either a monocular depth model or a per-clip 3D reconstruction, to recover the one axis a side-view camera cannot see. We present CopyQuad, which omits that stage and pins the missing axis to the robot's own stance width instead. The setting is side-view footage of sagittally dominated motion, where limb motion is almost entirely in the image plane. A frozen 2D keypoint detector and a fixed analytic retargeting then turn a single uncalibrated clip into a robot reference whose foot targets are reachable by construction, so no per-clip trajectory optimization is needed. One phase-indexed reward structure, whose only per-behavior freedom is three scalars from a shared sweep, learns a dog walk, a horse walk, a horse trot and two non-periodic gestures, all deployed zero-shot on hardware. We then measure what omitting the axis costs. In a training-free rigidity test, a video depth model varies the distance between the animal's hips by $40$ to $107\%$ of its own mean and a single-image metric model by $22$ to $58\%$, though that distance cannot move. Motion capture puts the true lateral paw travel of a dog walk at $4.5$ cm peak to peak, a mean deviation near $1.4$ cm against the $3.5$ cm of lateral foot error our policies already leave, so the discarded axis sits below the pipeline's resolution. Depth repaired to feasibility never beats the constant, and the unrepaired estimates put the robot on the ground.
papers.title_ja: CopyQuad: 深度モデルなしで単一の側面動画から四足歩行スキルを転移
papers.summary_ja: 四足ロボットの動画模倣において、単眼深度モデルや3D再構成による軸復元を省略し、欠落軸をロボットのスタンス幅に固定する手法を提案する。凍結された2Dキーポイント検出器と解析的リターゲティングにより、未校正の1クリップから到達可能な足ターゲットを生成し、クリップごとの軌道最適化を不要にする。単一の報酬構造で犬や馬の歩行をゼロショットでハードウェアに展開し、深度モデルの誤差がロボットの制御解像度以下であることを検証した。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習とロボット制御の手法だが、LLMや軌道力学の関心とは遠い

papers.title: LACRM: LLM-Guided Mining of Directed Advertiser Competition Relationships in E-Commerce Advertising
papers.summary: In e-commerce advertising, ad platforms typically fail to model the externalities among advertisers when making optimization decisions: an advertiser's actual performance is largely shaped by rivals competing for the same users; these rivals typically operate in overlapping product categories and at comparable budget scales. However, capturing this rivalry as an explicit, reusable signal is challenging because it is directed, multi-faceted, and partially observable. Existing paradigms such as interaction graphs, taxonomy rules, and single-embedding models do not fully capture these properties. In this paper, we propose LACRM (LLM-driven Advertiser Competition Relationship Mining), a novel framework that constructs directed competition graphs with continuous edge intensities via a three-stage pipeline. LACRM moves beyond symmetric similarity through LLM-driven role-separated profiling, which enables asymmetric multi-route retrieval to uncover both realized and latent rivals. The framework further incorporates listwise learning-to-rank aligned with temporal auction behavior to accurately model directed competition intensity. In offline retrieval experiments on an industrial benchmark, LACRM outperforms strong directed GNN baselines and ablation variants. Multi-LLM and human studies provide complementary evidence that the recovered latent rivals reflect meaningful market competition rather than merely model-generated artifacts. In production A/B tests, LACRM-guided bidding and incentive allocation increase advertising revenue by 1.73% and 1.14%, respectively. papers.title: MRFlow: Mechanism-Structured Residual Flow Matching for Virtual Cell Perturbation Prediction
papers.summary: Predicting cellular responses to chemical and genetic perturbations is a central test for AI virtual cells, yet many single-cell models reduce each condition to an average expression shift. This target is misaligned with perturbation biology: rare states, resistant subpopulations, and context-dependent effect sizes may coexist under the same intervention. MRFlow treats virtual-cell prediction as conditional transport between empirical single-cell measures. Control and perturbed cells are embedded in a variational latent state space, greedy low-cost supervision is constructed over detached minibatch states, and a conditional flow-matching vector field transports control populations toward perturbed populations. The field decomposes into a mechanism-structured affine dictionary, which recombines shared latent response operators with a low-rank condition-specific correction, and a spectrally controlled residual field for nonlinear cell-level variation. Genetic perturbations are encoded through a regulatory-graph GCN, chemical perturbations through Morgan fingerprints, and both enter the same conditional dynamics interface. Across eight gene and drug perturbation benchmarks, MRFlow attains the highest composite score while preserving competitive raw performance on differential-expression and distributional metrics. The results support latent distribution transport as a principled and empirically effective formulation for perturbation-aware virtual cell modeling.

papers.title: From Prototype to Massing: Learning Graph Correspondence for Scalable Facade Modeling
papers.summary: Facade articulation at building scale is usually resolved manually or through parametric systems that encode design intent as explicit rules. This paper investigates a complementary workflow in which a designer-authored prototype supplies transferable articulation logic. Prototype and target massing are represented as heterogeneous attributed graphs, and a Siamese graph attention network with instance-local triplet supervision embeds their segments in a shared metric space. Many-to-one nearest-neighbor retrieval then routes prototype Patterns to the larger target. On the original 85/15 within-corpus holdout, prototype-to-massing top-1 accuracy reached 96.5%, compared with a reported 76.5% raw-feature baseline. A Rhino demonstrator converts predicted correspondence into reusable facade Patterns, and qualitative applications on four built projects show the workflow across distinct massing organizations. The contribution is not automated facade generation, but an authoring model in which resolved geometry serves as a computational specification for project-scale propagation.

papers.title: An updated view of Jupiter's UV main auroral emission: large-scale analysis of UV and particle data from Juno's first 60 orbits
papers.summary: The properties and origins of Jupiter's UV main auroral emission are, at present, not yet fully understood, particularly the extent to which its two distinct zones, the Zone-I and Zone-II aurora, originate from a common source. In this work, remote-sensing and in-situ data from the Juno spacecraft are used to investigate and produce maps of the average properties of the main emission over Juno's first 60 orbits. It is found that the peak in mean energy of electrons precipitating in the main emission is consistently poleward of the energy-flux (or brightness) peak, in both hemispheres and at all local times, and is co-located with the statistical location of the Zone-II aurora. Evidence is presented that the flux-energy relationship of the main emission is adequately characterised by theoretical power laws describing electron acceleration from quasi-static potentials or Alfv\'enic turbulence and that it shows a modulation with ionospheric electron density consistent with theoretical predictions. Finally, the average energy spectra of precipitating electrons in the Zone-I aurora remain power-law-like between an energy flux of 1 and 100 mW m$^{-2}$, whereas the average Zone-II spectra develop a distinct ``plateau'' or ``flattop'' shape beyond an energy flux of $\sim$5 mW m$^{-2}$. Our results provide some evidence that the Zone-I and Zone-II aurorae are phenomenologically distinct, and the consequences of this interpretation for future investigation of the main emission are discussed.

papers.title: NAS Timers for Non-Terrestrial Networks: Current Standards and Directions
papers.summary: Response-supervision timers in the 5G Non-Access Stratum (NAS) bound the time allowed for signaling exchanges before retransmission or abnormal-case handling begins. In non-terrestrial networks, that interval can include satellite propagation, terrestrial transport, and processing by multiple core-network functions. Under current 3GPP specifications, the applicable timer value for satellite access is selected according to the satellite NG-RAN radio access technology (RAT) type. However, control paths within the same low Earth orbit (LEO) network can differ in propagation delay and processing load. This article reviews the relevant 3GPP timer semantics and traces the delay components covered by different timers through 5G registration. It organizes candidate refinements along two dimensions: configuration granularity and information scope. A registration case study illustrates the trade-off between avoiding premature timer expiry and recovering promptly from message loss. The article identifies the information and coordination that future specifications would need to address to support interoperable timer configuration.

papers.title: DShuttleNet: A Badminton Doubles Dataset for Evaluating Team Coordination
papers.summary: Most existing sports datasets are individual-centric or ball-centric, focusing on individual player actions while ignoring interactions among teammates. In badminton doubles, tactical success is governed by rapid team formation and coordination, yet standard resources for modeling these player interactions are scarce. To bridge this gap, we present DShuttleNet, a comprehensive dataset for badminton doubles curated from elite BWF World Tour tournaments. Beyond trajectory data, DShuttleNet uniquely incorporates expert-labeled "Loss Reasons," transforming the dataset into a diagnostic tool for causal tactical evaluation. We formally define two geometry-driven representations, Teammate-Relative Angle (TRA) and Vertical Shot Angle (VSA), to characterize coordination and shot aggressiveness. To quantify interpersonal synergy, we introduce novel metrics, Court Coverage Efficacy Index (CCEI) and Threat Load Asymmetry Index (TLAI), which evaluate the often-overlooked non-hitting partner's role and defensive coordination. Experimental results demonstrate that conventional models suffer from underfitting when failing to incorporate these coordination-centric features, highlighting the critical importance and potential impact of releasing DShuttleNet. Dataset is available at: https://doi.org/10.34740/kaggle/dsv/16097938.

papers.title: Building Trustworthy Household Robots through Open-World Safety
papers.summary: Foundation models are expanding robot capabilities, enabling robots to handle more diverse objects, follow sophisticated instructions, and operate in complex environments. These advances bring us to a future in which robots become part of everyday household life. However, cluttered, dynamic household environments also expose robots to unfamiliar objects, tasks, and interactions, making reliable zero-shot task completion an ongoing challenge for robotics research. From a security perspective, we argue for open-world safety: household robots should preserve specified safety requirements in unseen situations, including when they cannot complete the requested task. Safety protections must account for context and interactions that persist across actions and tasks. In this position paper, we examine why existing safety methods can fail to provide this protection. Protection can fail through misinterpreted context, overlooked past interactions, or stopping and recovery strategies that become unsafe under unfamiliar conditions. We therefore propose a research agenda to specify, learn, and ground safety requirements, enforce them with reliable recovery, and evaluate the generalization of such protections. We call for household robots whose safety protections remain reliable beyond the situations, context, and history used to train and develop them, to achieve open-world safety.
